options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians injured in police-reported crashes
options.denominator: No denominator; count of injured pedestrians
options.reason: Injury counts show how many pedestrians were hurt each year, a direct and widely understood measure of harm.
options.answer: Brooklyn recorded 2,835 pedestrians injured in 2025, down 22.1% from 3,641 in 2013, though injuries have risen from the 2020 low.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the number of pedestrians hurt each year has improved: the count was lower in 2025 than in 2013, but it has climbed since 2020. Annual injury counts are a direct measure of reported harm; they do not show injury risk per pedestrian or account for changes in walking volume.

options.metric: Annual count of pedestrians killed in police-reported crashes
options.denominator: No denominator; count of pedestrian deaths
options.reason: Fatality counts isolate the most severe outcome and prevent it from being obscured by the larger number of nonfatal injuries.
options.answer: Brooklyn recorded 39 pedestrian deaths in 2025, 30% more than the 30 deaths in 2013, despite year-to-year fluctuations.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual number of pedestrian deaths has improved: it was higher in 2025 than in 2013, with substantial variation between years. Fatality counts capture the most severe reported outcome, but without pedestrian exposure they cannot establish whether an individual pedestrian’s risk changed.
